task.description: REVIEWER hard gate (WF-02 Step 2d) on REQ-162's implementation, commit e937135 on lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex (SECURITY-REVIEWER already PASSed at commit 12d3b3e). Gate on idiomatic OTP usage, supervision integrity, scope creep, and decision-record consistency. Read the approved design (lib/letflow/design/req162-lua-script-error-capture.md), the real diff (git show e937135 -- lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex), and the current full file before verdict. Pay particular attention to: (1) whether making build_script_error/3 public (marked @doc false) as a test seam is idiomatic for this codebase or should instead be a private function tested indirectly/via a different mechanism -- check if this file or others in this codebase have an established convention for testing private functions; (2) whether the new handle_yield_result/3 clause and @spec extensions are cleanly integrated with no dead code or stale references (mirroring the exact class of defect REVIEWER found on REQ-161's first pass); (3) whether this diff has any ripple effect on other modules/tests given executor.ex is a heavily shared module.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation matches the approved design's specified control flow (design sections 1-6) -- no invented mechanism replacing what was approved.

build_script_error/3's public-for-testing pattern is idiomatic for this codebase -- check whether other modules in this file or elsewhere establish this same test-seam convention, or whether a different approach (e.g. testing via the public run_script/3 entry point only) would be more idiomatic; if the public function is kept, confirm its @doc false and narrow purpose are clearly documented so a future reader doesn't mistake it for a stable public API.

The new handle_yield_result/3 clause and both execute_with_manifest @spec extensions are cleanly integrated -- no stale references to the old bare {:error, String.t()} shape left anywhere in comments/moduledoc/other clauses that should have been updated.

No scope creep: nothing touched outside lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex and test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs (this requirement's owned_modules); platform.ex/capabilities.ex/sandbox.ex untouched, per design's explicit deferral.
Decision-record consistency: confirm nothing in this diff contradicts decision 0014 or REQ-148/157/161's own established conventions.
Moduledoc's new REQ-162 section accurately describes the mechanism, the branch (a)/(b) instruction-count finding, the 5-arm distinction, and the inherited capability-wiring gap -- no overstatement.
Confirm no ripple effect on other test files that exercise run_script/3/execute_with_manifest/2,3 -- run the full test suite yourself, don't just trust ELIXIR-DEV's report of 2283 passed.
mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix format --check-formatted both independently re-run by REVIEWER.
